title: How skills apply
description: Understand installed instructions, project rules, supporting resources, and optional agents.

children: A skill is a directory of instructions that an agent reads for a task. It does not execute application code or configure your formatter by itself.

CLI puts instruction files where your selected agent can read them. Installing

with a package manager makes the package files available, but does not activate those instructions in an agent. The npm package also exposes metadata and a schema for tooling; it has no JavaScript runtime entry point.
Native discovery depends on the agent's version and configuration. Explicit links in project instructions make task requirements clear: naming a public function calls for

Current user instructions take precedence over repository guidance, and repository guidance takes precedence over shared defaults. Existing projects retain their established vocabulary, toolchain, and framework choices. Project-specific exceptions belong in project instructions so they remain visible when installed skills are updated.
A skill requirement and authorization to act are separate. Reading
before a Git decision does not authorize a commit or push. Coding conventions describe the expected style, while configured and verified project tools provide automatic enforcement.
